title: Where great startup ideas come from: Airbnb, Coinbase and Stripe
summary: Dalton Caldwell and Michael Seibel unpack why Airbnb, Coinbase and Stripe worked. Each entered a market with bad incumbents, built something 10x better, was told by experts it was a dumb idea, and found the market bigger than they first thought. The lessons: ignore incumbents and non-user experts, build for users you know, and be careful with market-size math.

principles.text: Don't be scared off by an existing product. If its users hate it, a 10x better version is the opening.
principles.quote: you shouldn't give a [ __ ] if there's an existing product in the market if you're a user of that product or your friends or users of that product and they all hate it

principles.text: Ignore experts who aren't users and have never felt the pain of the existing product.
principles.quote: you should not give a [ __ ] if most of the people around you who you believe are experts don't think this is a good idea especially you shouldn't care if they're not going to be users

principles.text: Be skeptical of your own market size math. A 10x better product unlocks use cases you can't foresee.
principles.quote: be very careful about pretending that you know how big the market could be it turns out with so many of these transformational technologies there are use cases you can't dream of

principles.text: If your smart technical friends all complain about the same thing, that's a strong hint for an idea.
principles.quote: if all of your smart technical friends are complaining about the same thing maybe it's a real problem

principles.text: Stripe won developers by building what a programmer would want: beautiful site and docs, plus a scarce beta invite.
principles.quote: constantly ask themselves and push themselves to say what would i want or what would it what would a programmer want

principles.text: Pricing high can signal a real insight. Stripe was the most expensive option and people were still desperate for it.
principles.quote: they didn't give it away for free they didn't price it comparably they made it more expensive and people were still desperate to use it
